records.title: Controlled DOCX export still has no document-control header/footer, page x of y, TOC or house style, and defaults to A4; only the uncontrolled working copy got a DRAFT banner header/footer
records.evidenceAtHead: Code: server/services/authoring/authoring-export.ts renderDocx (388-492). The Document at 464-486 sets only numbering, footnotes and sections; there are no styles, no features.updateFields and no TableOfContents. The sections ternary at 475-485 attaches headers and footers ONLY when args.workingCopy is set, and they hold only the DRAFT banner text (no PageNumber). A controlled export is `{ children }`, with no section properties, header, footer or page size. A grep of server/ for TableOfContents|PageNumber matches only legacy generators (docx/docxFactory.ts, universal-packager.ts, biotech-artifact-generator.ts, templateExtractor.ts, common/exportFormats.mjs), none of them on the authoring export path. Both callers use renderAuthoringExport: the POST /docs/:docId/export route (authoring.router.ts:6651) and file-to-vault (authoring-file-to-vault.ts:426). git diff 92ccdba1 HEAD on the two audited files changes only the working-copy banner, the XML figure placeholders and PDF fallback tracking. Command: a tsx probe called renderAuthoringExport on an APPROVED doc (id D1, version 4) with a stub executor and unzipped the result. Controlled: headerParts [], footerParts [], tocField false, PAGE/NUMPAGES fields false, settings updateFields false, doc id and version not in document.xml, pgSz w:w=11906 w:h=16838 (A4). Working copy: header1.xml and footer1.xml present (banner only), still no TOC, no PAGE/NUMPAGES, A4. The audited version (git show 92ccdba1) had sections: [{ children }], so the original finding was correct. The PDF path has the same gap: renderers.ts:383-387 is page.pdf format 'A4' with no page numbers unless pageBanner is set.
records.remaining: Everything the finding names is still missing from the controlled (filing) DOCX: a header with title, document ID, version and status; a footer with confidentiality text and 'Page X of Y'; a TOC field; Template Library/house styles; and a Letter page size for an FDA pilot. The working copy added in 1a8ebb3ae has a header and footer, but they carry only the 'DRAFT — uncontrolled copy · id · vN · status' banner, with no page numbers and no TOC. That banner is an uncontrolled-copy marker, not a document-control header. The Template Library's style-driven generator (docxFactory.generateRegulatory with templateSpecToDocxStyle) already has header, footer and page-x-of-y logic, but authoring export does not use it.
records.severityRationale: This is not a security, tenant-isolation or data-integrity exposure, so it is not P0. But every controlled export a pilot user produces lacks the per-page document identification and page numbering that ICH M4 CTD organisation expects, and it renders on A4 for a US FDA pilot. The user has to rework each file in Word. Once a controlled export is edited, its bytes no longer match the artifactSha256 the export record attests (authoring-export.ts §11.10(b) hash). So the file the customer circulates or files is no longer the controlled record. Pilot users would rely on this output in production, so it must be fixed before then.
records.humanTestingNote: Freeze or approve an Authoring document, then choose Download > 'Controlled export (Word)'. The .docx opens with no header or footer, no page numbers, no table of contents, Word default styles and an A4 page. 'Controlled export (PDF)' is also A4 with no page numbers. 'Working copy (Word)' shows the bold 'DRAFT — uncontrolled copy · <id> · v<N> · <STATUS> · downloaded … by …' line at the top and bottom of each page, but still no page numbers or TOC. The journey completes. Log this as one known gap rather than a bug per document. Workaround: add the header, footer and TOC by hand in Word, but the edited file no longer matches the export-history record's SHA-256.
records.instructions: 1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (Rule 0). Write the failing test first: add server/services/authoring/__tests__/authoring-export-docx-layout.test.ts. It calls renderAuthoringExport (authoring-export.ts:565) with a stub executor `{ query: async () => ({ rows: [], rowCount: 0 }) }`, doc `{ id:'D1', title:'Clinical Overview', status:'APPROVED', version:4 }`, two sections with codes 2.5.1/2.5.2, format 'docx' and signatures []. Unzip it with JSZip (as server/routes/__tests__/authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts:112-125 does) and assert: a word/header*.xml containing 'D1', 'Version 4' and 'APPROVED'; a word/footer*.xml containing both a PAGE and a NUMPAGES field; document.xml containing a TOC field instruction (`TOC \o "1-3"`); word/settings.xml containing updateFields; and ` · Document ID · Version · ', with spec.header.text appended when set. Footer: confidentiality text (spec.brand.confidentialityNotice or spec.footer.text), then a TextRun with children ['Page ', PageNumber.CURRENT, ' of ', PageNumber.TOTAL_PAGES] (docx 9.7.1 supports this). When a banner is passed (working copy), add the bold banner as its own paragraph in BOTH header and footer, so the assertions at authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts:112-125 keep passing. 5. In renderDocx, replace the sections ternary (authoring-export.ts:475-485) with ONE section that always has `properties: { page: { size from style.page, margin: style.margins, pageNumbers: { start: 1 } } }` and the helper's headers and footers, passing banner: args.workingCopy?.banner. Do not remove the working-copy banner, and keep the working copy's missing signature manifestation (lines 451-461) unchanged. 6. Still in renderDocx, insert a 'Table of Contents' paragraph and `new docxNs.TableOfContents('Table of Contents', { hyperlink: true, headingStyleRange: '1-3' })` after the title and notice paragraphs (after line ~401). Section headings are already HEADING_1 (authoring-blocks-to-docx.ts:263). Add `features: { updateFields: true }` to the Document at line 464 so Word fills the TOC and page fields on open. Also add `styles: { default: { document: { run: { font: style.fonts.body, size: style.fontSizes.body } } }, paragraphStyles: Heading1-3 from style.fonts.heading / fontSizes.heading1-3 }`. 7. PDF parity, so the DOCX and PDF of one record agree (the module's stated invariant at prepareShared, authoring-export.ts:225-231). Extend PdfRenderOptions (server/export/renderers.ts:356) with `headerLine?`, `footerLine?` and `pageNumbers?: boolean`, and `format: 'Letter'|'A4'`. In renderHtmlToPdfTracked (369-395), set displayHeaderFooter with the lines plus ` of `. In renderFallbackPdf, stamp 'Page i of n' with the existing bufferPages loop (renderers.ts ~511-522). Pass these from renderPdf (authoring-export.ts:498-561). 8. House-style selection (shared with CAT1-16): accept an optional `templateId` in the bodies of POST /docs/:docId/export (authoring.router.ts:6539), POST /docs/:docId/working-copy (~6700) and file-to-vault. Resolve it with getTemplate(tenantId, id) (server/services/templates/templateStore.ts:173), which is tenant-scoped. An unknown or other-tenant id fails closed with 404 TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND before any audit or export row is written; never fall back silently to the default. Pass the normalized spec as `formatting`. Record templateId and a SHA-256 of the normalized spec in logExport metadata (router ~6680) and in the WORKING_COPY audit payload (~6735). 9. Client: in client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DownloadMenu.tsx, offer the org's active templates (GET /api/c2c/templates) as an optional 'Formatting' choice. Send templateId with both the controlled export and the working copy. 'Default (Letter)' sends nothing. 10. Re-run the step-1 test (now green), authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts and authoring-export-xml-figures.test.ts. Add negative cases: another tenant's templateId gives 404 with no export row written, and a spec with bodyFont 'Arial' shows up in word/styles.xml. Commit on concept2cure-v2 with the failing-first evidence named in the message.
records.acceptance: (a) Failing-first: the new authoring-export-docx-layout.test.ts is shown failing at HEAD (no header/footer parts, no PAGE/NUMPAGES field, no TOC, pgSz 11906x16838) before the change, and passing after it. (b) A controlled DOCX export of an APPROVED document has a header on every page with title, document ID, version and status, and a footer with confidentiality text and 'Page X of Y' (PAGE and NUMPAGES fields). It has a TOC field over Heading 1-3 that Word populates on open (settings updateFields=true), Letter page size by default, and default/heading fonts from the template spec. (c) The working-copy DOCX has the same header and footer plus the bold DRAFT banner top and bottom and no signature manifestation; authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts passes unchanged. (d) The PDF of the same document shows the same header line and 'Page X of Y' on every page, in both the Puppeteer and fallback renderers. (e) With a templateId, the spec's fonts, margins, header and footer text appear in the DOCX, and templateId and the spec hash are recorded on the export row and the WORKING_COPY audit row. Another tenant's or an unknown templateId returns 404 and writes no export or audit row. (f) File-to-vault output (authoring-file-to-vault.ts renderForVaultFiling) carries the same header and footer, because it uses the same renderer.
records.dependencies: CAT1-16 (template choice on export; its draft-export half is now delivered by POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/working-copy). Founder decisions: default page size (Letter recommended for the FDA-only pilot; report open question 2) and default confidentiality text. PDF parity needs the Puppeteer engine available in the AWS image (otherwise the plain-text fallback is used and only stamps the lines).
